title: The Fire Kasina: Questions and Answers on Retreat with Practice Notes and Commentary
author: Shannon Stein and Daniel M. Ingram
edition_cited: Brighton: Heptarchia, first edition October 2017 (authors' free PDF, archive.org OCR)
tradition: Modern pragmatic-dharma kasina practice, drawing on the Visuddhimagga and Vimuttimagga
locator_hints: Introductory chapters: Ingram's own account of starting with a candle flame; what a kasina is ('an external support used to generate an after-image')
Basic instruction (file line c. 1082): 'Sit comfortably and stare at the flame for a minute or...' then close the eyes and attend to the after-image, favouring 'anything resembling a red dot'
Q&A on the phase after the red and black dot, 'the murk' (line c. 1643-1745), and how images organise out of it
Q&A on carrying the after-image off the cushion and eyes-open after-images (line c. 1557-1575, 1799-1835), including using an LED or other light source
Mapping of the red dot, murk and later phases onto jhanas (line c. 2231 ff.)
Day-by-day retreat journal, Days One to Twenty-Five
Appendix on candle safety and practical set-up (line c. 6335)
summary: A 25-day solo candle-flame retreat journal by Shannon Stein with Daniel Ingram's answers to her daily questions. The basic instruction is to stare at a candle flame for about a minute, close the eyes, and take the retinal after-image as the object, giving most attention to anything like a red dot; when it fades, open the eyes and repeat. The authors describe a reproducible sequence: the red dot, its change to a black or green dot with coloured surround, then 'the murk', a shapeless field said to be where real progress is made and out of which detailed, self-moving, coloured imagery later forms. Ingram answers practical questions on how long to stare, widening attention around the dot, what to do when nothing but murk is present, carrying the after-image into walking and eyes-open periods, using other light sources, and the fear and energetic side effects. The journal records what was seen each day.
why_relevant: The fullest modern first-person account of taking a flame after-image through to self-sustaining seen imagery, with troubleshooting for each stall point and time scales in days.
